meta.title: Guest Welcome: Render Data Safely
meta.subtitle: Review browser rendering code, use context-appropriate output handling and catch a second XSS pattern.

brief.role: You are reviewing a fictional front-end change that renders a guest-provided display name.
brief.context: The change works for friendly text, but it uses a browser API that interprets strings as markup. Inspect the evidence, choose a safe rendering approach and verify a similar helper did not reintroduce the problem.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. The scenario uses fictional names and code. Do not put guest or sensitive data into browser test fixtures or AI prompts.

mission.objective: Ensure untrusted values are displayed as data in the right browser context rather than interpreted as executable markup.

achievements.title: XSS reviewer
achievements.description: Completed the review without using a hint.

achievements.title: Context recall
achievements.description: Recognized unsafe markup insertion in a second UI component.

stages.title: Find the browser write that can execute untrusted content
stages.instruction: Select the line that sends a guest-provided value to a markup-interpreting browser API.
hints: Consider whether the API treats the display name as text or as browser markup.
Find the write that uses innerHTML with the untrusted value.

feedback.correct: You found the unsafe browser write. The value may look like a name, but it is still untrusted input until it is handled for its output context.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the line that gives an untrusted value to an API that interprets markup.

feedbackByMissing.welcome-view:3: innerHTML parses its string as markup. Do not join an untrusted display name into markup or an attribute template.

concept.label: Render untrusted output for its destination context

stages.title: Choose the safe rendering approach
stages.instruction: Choose the correction that preserves the greeting without treating the display name as executable markup.

choices.label: Replace angle brackets manually and keep using innerHTML
choices.detail: Maintain a small list of characters to escape.
choices.feedback: Hand-rolled escaping is easy to get wrong and does not generalize across HTML, attributes, JavaScript, URLs and CSS.

choices.label: Render the value as text, or use the framework's trusted encoder for the exact output context
choices.detail: Use textContent when markup is unnecessary; use the framework's context-aware mechanism when it is required.

choices.label: Keep the markup write and rely only on Content-Security-Policy
choices.feedback: A Content-Security-Policy is useful defence in depth, but it does not make unsafe rendering an acceptable primary control.

hints: The best primary defence makes the browser treat the name as data.
Choose the option that avoids hand-built escaping and matches handling to the output context.

feedback.correct: The correction makes the browser display the value as data. Trusted framework encoders are the alternative when a specific markup context is genuinely needed.
feedback.incorrect: That approach still relies on fragile escaping or on a secondary control instead of safely handling the output.

concept.label: Use a browser API that treats untrusted values as text

stages.title: Run the simulated browser-safety checks
stages.instruction: Verify the changed component and inspect the remaining helper finding before you clear the review.

results.message: The display name is rendered as text instead of interpreted markup.
The welcome component still sends an untrusted value to a markup parser.
The shared notice helper still writes its message through innerHTML.

feedback.failed: The changed component is safer, but a reusable helper repeats the same pattern. Inspect it before approving the merge.

stages.title: Find the rendering regression in the shared helper
stages.instruction: Select the line that repeats the unsafe browser-write pattern in this different component.
hints: The helper's message can be untrusted too.
Look for the API that parses message text as markup.

feedback.correct: You applied the same output-handling rule in a new component. Reusable UI code needs the same context-aware protection as a feature-specific view.
feedback.incorrect: The unsafe line gives the message to innerHTML instead of rendering it as text.

feedbackByMissing.notice-helper:2: The helper passes the message to innerHTML. Use a text-rendering API or a trusted context-aware renderer.

concept.label: Render untrusted output for its destination context

completion.title: Guest text stays data, not markup
completion.message: You removed unsafe rendering from the feature, verified the result and recognized the same XSS pattern in a shared helper.
takeaways: Untrusted input can be dangerous when it is displayed, not only when it is received.
Choose output handling for the exact destination: HTML text, attribute, JavaScript, URL or CSS.
Use trusted framework encoders and defence-in-depth controls instead of hand-rolled escaping.
